newsitem.title: USA: New Dow components get a lift.
newsitem.headline: New Dow components get a lift.

text.p: The four stocks to be added to the 30-stock Dow Jones industrial average rose in early trading Thursday amid demand from mutual funds and other institutional investors, traders said.

After Wednesday's market close, Dow Jones & Co. Inc., the publisher of the Wall Street Journal, announced that computer maker Hewlett-Packard Co., insurance firm Travelers Group Inc., health products company Johnson & Johnson and top retailer Wal-Mart Stores Inc. will replace four existing companies in the average as of Monday.
Wal-Mart, Hewlett-Packard and Johnson & Johnson were among the most active stocks on the New York Stock Exchange in morning trading.
Johnson & Johnson was up 50 cents at $60.125, Hewlett-Packard gained $1 to $55.625, Travelers rose 37.5 cents to $55, and Wal-Mart gained 50 cents to $29.25.

Among the stocks knocked out of the index, Texaco Inc. dropped $1.75 to $101, Westinghouse Electric Corp. was unchanged at $19, Woolworth Corp. was off 25 cents at $22.75, and Bethlehem Steel Corp. was off 12.5 cents at $8.625.
Overall, the Dow was off 45.03 points at 6,994.34 in morning trading after earlier falling more than 50 points.
